answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. The key insight is that coordination itself leaks: the more unified a farm is, the more easily its shared style or timing betrays it. The effect is that voting power tracks real contribution, so a flood of accounts cannot outvote a smaller set of genuinely established participants. Consider a grove as the anchor of the cost.
